subject: 20260913-183723-sweep-deepgram-30
headline: The agent demonstrates high task success and steady median latency up to 40 concurrent calls, but tail latency spikes severely on the final turn.

insights.title: Spiking Tail Latency on the Final Turn
insights.finding: The p95 response time (time to first audio) on the final turn (turn 5) spikes to 3181.8 milliseconds, even though its median (p50) is very low at 736.3 milliseconds.
insights.why_it_matters: A delay of over 3 seconds when ending a call can cause callers to think the system hung up or disconnected, spoiling the user experience right at the end.
insights.next_step: Profile the conversation-ending turn in the agent logs to find why the tail latency is disproportionately slow.

insights.title: Transient Latency Anomaly Rather than Capacity Exhaustion
insights.finding: The p95 time to first audio spiked to 1939.9 milliseconds at concurrency 5, but then decreased to 1252.6 milliseconds at concurrency 10, 985.5 milliseconds at concurrency 20, and 1029.2 milliseconds at concurrency 40.
insights.why_it_matters: A slowdown that rises and then falls back as calls increase was not caused by load, pointing instead to a transient host or network issue during the second step.
insights.next_step: Check the system logs for step c5 to see if any backend cold-starts or network route changes occurred.

insights.title: Tail Latency Breaks while Median Holds Flat under Load
insights.finding: The median response time (p50) holds steady between 781.8 milliseconds at baseline and 784.7 milliseconds at maximum load (c40). However, the tail latency (p99) remains highly elevated at 3166.9 milliseconds at baseline and 3116.2 milliseconds at c40.
insights.why_it_matters: While the typical caller experiences consistent, fast responses under load, the worst-case tail latency is broken even at a single caller, suggesting a persistent optimization issue rather than load-induced queueing.
insights.next_step: Investigate the slowest single-user calls at baseline to understand why 1% of turns take more than 3 seconds.

insights.title: Thinking Process is the Primary Latency Bottleneck
insights.finding: At the highest load of 40 concurrent calls, the median thinking and speaking time (think_speak p50) is 490.5 milliseconds, which is much larger than the median endpointing time of 300.7 milliseconds and the median network round trip of 83.3 milliseconds.
insights.why_it_matters: The agent's internal processing (deciding what to say and generating the response) is the largest contributor to the caller's wait, meaning optimization efforts should focus on model response time.
insights.next_step: Optimize the LLM prompt and speech generation pipelines to decrease the median thinking time.

insights.title: High Task Success Over a Small Judged Sample
insights.finding: The automated judge evaluated only 20 calls out of 210 total calls and passed all 20 of them, resulting in a 100.0% pass rate.
insights.why_it_matters: While a 100.0% pass rate is highly encouraging, the evaluation sample is less than 10% of the total run, which means rare conversational failures might not be captured.
insights.next_step: Increase the judge sample size in future tests to evaluate a larger portion of the generated calls.

insights.title: Strong Performance Against Observed Industry Standards
insights.finding: The median response latency of 784.7 milliseconds at maximum load is well below the Hamming observed production median of 1400 milliseconds, though it remains slower than the human conversational marker of 300 milliseconds.
insights.why_it_matters: The typical user experience is highly competitive and faster than many production implementations, although it does not yet match natural human conversational speed.
insights.next_step: Aim to reduce the gap between the agent's median latency and the natural human turn-taking standard.
